title: appointments.slots.hold payload
description: Sets a slot aside while somebody DECIDES on a pending booking request (appointments#69). It is a lease, not a booking: it has no appointment number, it is not in the agenda, and it frees itself. Note what this payload does NOT accept: the expiry. The TTL is decided server-side from `appointments_settings.hold_minutes` (15 min by default, 0 = holds switched off), which is the rule Google Actions Center writes down for its `Lease` — the caller may propose a lifetime and the server may shorten it if it is excessive. Here it is not even proposed: a caller choosing its own expiry could set a whole agenda aside for a month.

source.description: Who is asking (`whatsapp_inbox`, or `manual` when a person sets the slot aside from the agenda). OPAQUE to this module: `appointments` never learns what a WhatsApp request is, only that someone identifiable set a slot aside and can give it back.

source_ref.description: Opaque reference to the asking row (the request id). Together with `source` it is the idempotency key: reopening the panel, or the outbox redelivering an event, MOVES this hold instead of leaving the previous one orphaned.

staff_id.description: The professional whose agenda is set aside. Empty = the whole agenda, same convention as a blocked time. A hold on one professional never closes another's diary, or setting one slot aside would empty the salon.

start_datetime.description: ISO-8601 start of the slot being set aside.

end_datetime.description: ISO-8601 end of the slot. `[start, end)`: a hold ending at 10:15 leaves 10:15 free, the same convention as the overlap gate.

label.description: What the agenda paints over the slot. Without a name, a slot that disappears reads as a bug — Square's own troubleshooting article lists its 15-minute hold among the causes of slots that «appear unavailable for no reason».
